title: Improve dedicated autoscaler: smoother burst controls, throughput guarantees, and utilization reporting
author: Sanjay Patel
release_notes: Improves Dedicated autoscaler stability and observability: smoother token-bucket burst behavior, tighter throughput guarantees for latency-sensitive routes, and richer fleet utilization reporting to help ops tune capacity.
description: Motivation: Customers on Dedicated have reported occasional latency spikes during synchronized request bursts and difficulty correlating those bursts with autoscaler behavior. This PR makes three focused changes: 1) implement token-bucket smoothing for burst allowances so short spikes don't immediately trigger large-scale scaling; 2) add a throughput-guarantee layer for latency-sensitive route classes that prefers reprovisioning lower-latency instances before scaling the entire fleet; 3) expand utilization reporting with per-fleet, per-pool histograms and retention-friendly rollups to help SREs tune policies. What changed (high level): token-bucket smoothing algorithm + config knobs; new throughput-guarantee scheduler layer with prioritization rules; metrics exporter changes and new observability dashboard queries; integration tests and canary config for Dedicated fleets. Checklist: - [x] Design doc (ENG-2374) reviewed; - [x] Unit + integration tests added; - [x] Canary plan + rollback policy documented; - [x] Observability dashboards updated; - [x] Release notes drafted. Related: ENG-2374, ENG-2401, SUP-4421. Deployment notes: Feature is gated behind a feature flag (dedicated.autoscaler.smoother_burst_v2) and defaults to off. The flag will be enabled in the canary region for targeted fleets first, and only rolled out cluster-wide after 72h of stable metrics. Backcompat: default autoscaler behavior unchanged unless the flag is enabled. Rollback: feature flag off immediately disables smoothing and returns to existing tokenbucket behavior. See linear tickets for rollout schedule and canary fleet names.

review_comments: Maya Chen: Nice end-to-end. A couple questions: what's the expected additional memory usage for per-pool histograms? Can we cap cardinality?

Sanjay Patel (author): We're using HDR histograms with configurable buckets; default retention rollup reduces cardinality and we cap active pools by default to 200 per-region. Added config knobs and docs.
